pageCoverage.sourceObservation: Printed 1. Lecture 31 title, Introduction to Computer Vision, instructor and institutional identification; no examinable content.
pageCoverage.exclusionReason: Printed 1. Lecture 31 title, Introduction to Computer Vision, instructor and institutional identification; no examinable content.

pageCoverage.sourceObservation: Printed 2. Learning outcomes list vision basics, human/digital differences and image formation. Administrative outline, not an additional technical proposition.
pageCoverage.exclusionReason: Printed 2. Learning outcomes list vision basics, human/digital differences and image formation. Administrative outline, not an additional technical proposition.

pageCoverage.sourceObservation: Printed 3. Contents list introduction/history/applications, light/human/machine vision, photometric and geometric formation. Outline only.
pageCoverage.exclusionReason: Printed 3. Contents list introduction/history/applications, light/human/machine vision, photometric and geometric formation. Outline only.

pageCoverage.sourceObservation: Printed 4. Six illustrated cards: perception identifies environment; localization estimates position/orientation through landmarks/odometry; manipulation uses visual/force feedback; interaction recognizes gestures/intent; navigation plans collision-free paths; inspection detects defects/wear.
pageCoverage.independentExaminableAngles: Six task distinctions, object perception versus pose, route selection, visual grasping/interaction and defect/wear inspection.

pageCoverage.sourceObservation: Printed 5. Vision seeks world properties from images, inverse to graphics rendering scene models. Shape, illumination and color distributions are named reconstruction goals; this is not a uniqueness guarantee.
pageCoverage.independentExaminableAngles: Vision versus graphics direction; nonunique inverse and shape/illumination ambiguity.

pageCoverage.sourceObservation: Printed 6. Eye/camera and brain/algorithm analogy. Arrows run lens plus CCD/CMOS sensor to image processing, feature extraction, ML models, then recognition, navigation/obstacle avoidance and manipulation.
pageCoverage.independentExaminableAngles: Eye/brain analogy and directed camera-processing-robot-task pipeline.

pageCoverage.sourceObservation: Printed 7. Projection loses depth and creates size-distance ambiguity. Cartoon contrasts semantic human labels with robot features, edges and uncertainty, not a proof that machine recognition is impossible.
pageCoverage.independentExaminableAngles: Size-distance ambiguity and interpretation beyond raw edge/features, without claiming recognition impossible.

pageCoverage.sourceObservation: Printed 8. Historical diagram: early line labels and flexible pictorial structures; Marr goal and method labels, with repeated heading instead of a clear third level. Middle: pyramids/scale-space, smoothness regularization, MRF probabilistic global optimization. Later: SfM reconstruction, HDR/panoramas/texture synthesis, deep learning. Grouping is not exact invention chronology.
pageCoverage.independentExaminableAngles: Line labeling, flexible pictorial parts, incomplete Marr goal/method list, multiresolution, regularization, MRF, SfM, computational photography and deep learning; no exact invention-date claim.

pageCoverage.sourceObservation: Printed 9. Industrial examples OCR, mechanical tolerance/defect inspection, CT/MRI analysis, autonomous systems/SLAM. Consumer examples stitching, AR reference tracking, biometric authentication and morphing/stabilization.
pageCoverage.independentExaminableAngles: OCR, mechanical inspection, medical CT/MRI, autonomous pose/mapping, panorama stitching, AR, biometrics and visual effects.

pageCoverage.sourceObservation: Printed 10. E(lambda) is intensity over wavelength; absorption changes spectrum. Visible range approximately 400–700 nm. Source dates Newton to 1670, not independently established here. Normalized plot has Sun 5778 K peaking near 500 nm and lamp 2600 K rising over shown 300–1000 nm domain; it cannot prove absolute power or lamp global peak at boundary.
pageCoverage.independentExaminableAngles: Spectral intensity and absorption, approximate 400–700 nm range, normalized/truncated Sun and lamp spectra, white-light dispersion; historical year excluded.

pageCoverage.sourceObservation: Printed 11. Simplified L(lambda)=E(lambda)R(lambda), 0<=R<=1; printed W m^-2 needs spectral/radiometric definitions. Diagram illuminant to reflecting surface to eye response. Rods are sensitive low-light intensity receptors; cones daylight/color; response integrates received spectrum times sensitivity.
pageCoverage.independentExaminableAngles: Illuminant/reflectance/received-light product, receptor weighting, zero-reflectance consequence, rods/cones, simplified units and illumination dependence.

pageCoverage.sourceObservation: Printed 12. Three overlapping L/M/S sensitivities, not disjoint wavelength bins; upper normalized peaks roughly 570/545/445 nm. Integrals rho/gamma/beta of L times M_r/M_g/M_b. Lower filled spectral-response plot has non-normalized different areas; do not conflate with upper sensitivity curves.
pageCoverage.independentExaminableAngles: Overlapping L/M/S sensitivities, weighted integrals, intensity scaling and information loss in three-channel reduction; normalized sensitivities versus unnormalized weighted areas need explicit comparison.

pageCoverage.sourceObservation: Printed 13. Tristimulus response triplet. Filled areas represent integrals for a red brick; L-cone area dominates, M intermediate and S smaller. Repeats lower figure from p932 but adds interpretation.
pageCoverage.independentExaminableAngles: Tristimulus triplet and area interpretation; dominant L-cone response in this brick example remains an untested incremental observation.

pageCoverage.sourceObservation: Printed 14. Pipeline arrows: real world -> optics (lens, aperture, shutter) -> CCD/CMOS -> ISO gain -> ADC -> demosaic -> denoise -> white balance -> gamma -> compress -> RGB. Sensor photosites are analogous to retina/cones; this is a simplified pipeline, not biological identity.
pageCoverage.independentExaminableAngles: Front-end pipeline order, directed ISP sequence, physical silicon photosites and retinal analogy.

pageCoverage.sourceObservation: Printed 15. Actual CCD diagram shifts charge to common output voltage conversion; CMOS diagram has local per-pixel conversion/amplification. Text expands CCD correctly; CMOS wording says Metal Oxide on Silicon, a terminology issue. Both convert photons to charge before different readout architectures.
pageCoverage.independentExaminableAngles: CCD charge transfer/common output versus local CMOS conversion, common sensing function and inaccurate printed CMOS expansion.

pageCoverage.sourceObservation: Printed 16. CFA over silicon photosites; Bayer 2x2 has two green, one red, one blue. Diagram gray underlying blocks are photosites, colored top squares filters. Responses overlap. Analog ISO gain amplifies sensed signal; ADC quantizes continuous voltage.
pageCoverage.independentExaminableAngles: Bayer pattern proportions, missing-channel count, wavelength-selective CFA, gain versus photon collection and explicitly supplied ADC quantization.

pageCoverage.sourceObservation: Printed 17. Demosaicing estimates two missing channels from neighbors. Denoising addresses shot noise/photon variance and thermal dark current. Sharpening applies edge enhancement for optical/demosaicing blur. It is not exact missing-data recovery or elimination of all noise.
pageCoverage.independentExaminableAngles: Demosaicing, stochastic photon/thermal noise, denoising and sharpening limitations.

pageCoverage.sourceObservation: Printed 18. White balance uses channel gains for neutral appearance; color correction uses 3x3 or 3x4 matrix to compensate sensor spectral differences toward XYZ/sRGB. Gamma is power-law response matching, followed by JPEG compression; color-correction C differs in purpose from geometric camera C.
pageCoverage.independentExaminableAngles: Neutral-patch gains, channel-mixing color correction, color versus geometric matrix C, gamma-like power law, compression and affine color example.

pageCoverage.sourceObservation: Printed 19. Reflected light is collected/focused; image formation projects 3D to 2D and loses depth. Diagram shows source, surface normal/reflection rays, optics, virtual image plane and rear sensor plane. Size/distance ambiguity repeats with explicit light-path model.
pageCoverage.independentExaminableAngles: Illumination/reflection, local normal versus viewing ray, rear sensor versus front virtual plane.

pageCoverage.sourceObservation: Printed 20. Pinhole small aperture forms inverted image on opposite wall; ideal model needs no focusing adjustment but image is dim. Ray diagram confirms inversion, not a lens or bright capture.
pageCoverage.independentExaminableAngles: Rear pinhole inversion, light-collection trade-off, ideal no-focus-adjustment model versus physical resolution/brightness limits.

pageCoverage.sourceObservation: Printed 21. Lens collects light over larger area and converges rays. Thin convex lens 1/|z_o|+1/|z_i|=1/f, appropriate real-object/real-image magnitudes. Diagram inverted real image and focal points. Human crystalline lens contrasted with compound camera lenses; eye also has other optical surfaces beyond this simplified sentence.
pageCoverage.independentExaminableAngles: Thin-lens equation, real-distance domain, focal limit, signed magnification, virtual-image sign convention and simplified lens comparison.

pageCoverage.sourceObservation: Printed 22. Virtual front image plane at distance f yields non-inverted coordinates. Similar triangles x=fX/Z, y=fY/Z with camera-frame coordinates. Homogeneous representation permits matrix multiplication, but Euclidean division remains.
pageCoverage.independentExaminableAngles: Front-plane signs, projective scaling ambiguity, linear homogeneous map versus nonlinear Cartesian division, numeric projection and Z=0 boundary.

pageCoverage.sourceObservation: Printed 23. Homogeneous image (fX,fY,Z), divide by last component; camera point (X,Y,Z,1). C is 3x4 [[f,0,0,0],[0,f,0,0],[0,0,1,0]]. World point transformed with inverse camera pose. Diagram distinguishes world O and camera C coordinate vectors.
pageCoverage.independentExaminableAngles: Matrix dimensions, homogeneous normalization/equivalence, inverse pose, translation and rotation ordering.

pageCoverage.sourceObservation: Printed 24. Discrete W by H photosite grid with pitches w,h; origin top-left, u right, v down, bounds depicted W-1 and H-1. Image point and optical-axis/principal-point geometry retained.
pageCoverage.independentExaminableAngles: Zero-based last index, right/down pixel axes and physical sensor size from pitch/count.

pageCoverage.sourceObservation: Printed 25. Principal point (u0,v0) is optical-axis intersection. Metric to pixels: u=x/w+u0, v=y/h+v0; homogeneous conversion has diag(1/w,1/h,1) and offset last column.
pageCoverage.independentExaminableAngles: Principal point versus pixel origin, anisotropic metric-to-pixel conversion, physical pitch versus homogeneous scale and pitch sensitivity.

pageCoverage.sourceObservation: Printed 26. K with f/w,f/h,u0,v0 times Q=[I|0], then inverse camera pose for world projection. Intrinsic and extrinsic factors explicitly separated. Printed rounding-to-nearest statement is an index-selection convention, not mandatory loss of subpixel coordinates. Camera C notation differs from earlier minimal camera-frame projection.
pageCoverage.independentExaminableAngles: Intrinsics/extrinsics, unit conversions, composition order, optional integer indexing, subpixel scope and combined pose/projection/visibility calculation.

pageCoverage.sourceObservation: Printed 27. Source point (.3,.4,5) m and f=.015 m produce (.0009,.0012) m; parenthetical (1.5,2.0) mm is inconsistent. Camera left .5 m gives (.0024,.0012). Pixel example rho=10e-6, image1280x1024, pp640/512 yields730/632. Missing SE3 import and library-default unit behavior require execution context checks.
pageCoverage.independentExaminableAngles: Metric/pixel projections, wrong metric-to-mm annotation, leftward camera/rightward image, missing SE3 context, calibration reassignment and constructor roles.

pageCoverage.sourceObservation: Printed 28. Visibility tests sensor bounds; regular frontal grid versus pose-dependent oblique distortion. Parallel world directions can have vanishing points, with image-parallel exceptions. Toolbox can project primitives such as cubes; bounds alone are not occlusion testing.
pageCoverage.independentExaminableAngles: Positive-depth and half-open sensor eligibility versus occlusion, oblique-grid depth variation and finite/infinite vanishing directions.

pageCoverage.sourceObservation: Printed 29. 3x3 grid side .2 centered at z=1. Frontal plot u~490/640/790 and v~362/512/662. Camera x=-.25 shifts u right by375 while v unchanged. Visibility example columns (0,0,10),(10,10,10),(.3,.4,5), returns pixel rows[640,2140,730],[512,2012,632] and true,false,true. These displayed outputs expose worked answers.
pageCoverage.independentExaminableAngles: Actual NumPy point-column layout, output/mask, centered grid and shift, execution order and explicitly supplied per-call pose override.

pageCoverage.sourceObservation: Printed 30. Cube side .2 centered z=1, camera translation x=-.25. Actual plots shift right and show depth-dependent horizontal displacement; corresponding near/far face sizes differ. Claim all coplanar edges remain parallel is overbroad; constant-depth face directions are the qualified case, depth directions converge.
pageCoverage.independentExaminableAngles: Cube-edge geometry, unequal-depth parallax, coplanar parallel-line counterexample, image-parallel exception and numeric finite vanishing point.

pageCoverage.sourceObservation: Printed 31. Summary repeats vision/inverse reconstruction, biological analogy, ambiguity, sensing pipeline and intrinsic/extrinsic projection. No new technical angle; wording about pinhole focusing is shorthand relative to p940.
Printed 32. Three references only: Szeliski, Corke and Litwiller. Bibliography, not additional course claims.
pageCoverage.exclusionReason: Printed 32. Three references only: Szeliski, Corke and Litwiller. Bibliography, not additional course claims.

pageCoverage.sourceObservation: Printed 33. Thank You closing page; no technical content.
pageCoverage.exclusionReason: Printed 33. Thank You closing page; no technical content.

meaningfulGaps.finding: No current item asks the learner to distinguish the upper independently normalized receptor-sensitivity curves from the lower weighted response-area plot, or identify the explicitly stated dominant L-cone response for the red-brick example. Q0932-Q01 checks overlap and Q0933-Q01 checks the generic meaning of the triplet, so neither requires the actual incremental plot/prose conclusion.
meaningfulGaps.target: Extend the existing brick/response figure item to assess L-dominant response from weighted area while not inferring equal channel responses from normalized peak heights. This is one bounded figure-interpretation gap, not a request for another numerical variant or exact peak-wavelength trivia.
meaningfulGaps.closureReason: Current new item distinguishes normalized sensitivity peaks from weighted response areas and identifies the displayed L-dominant red-brick example.

numericalVariantPolicy: Numeric substitutions and repeated projection outputs do not inflate the 27 concept records. Pose-only, projection-only and combined synthesis items were retained as distinct examination operations.

sourceIssuesPreserved.note: All issue records unchanged. Historical-date context was not independently adjudicated; the date is explicitly excluded from the quiz. Source errors are preserved, not silently corrected.

limitations: Twelve source annotations preserved; the disputed historical year is excluded, not independently adjudicated.
Official API source inspected; complete machinevisiontoolbox runtime not executed.
